neighbours.label: Practising or performing music on an instrument: fires on or just after the performing verb (strumming his guitar, playing the accordion, improve her tone), not on playing sports or games
fire: Every evening the old sailor sat on the quay playing the concertina for anyone who would listen.
My cousin practises the clarinet for an hour a day because she wants to improve her breathing.
A young woman stood by the fountain strumming her ukulele and humming along.
He joined the town band at sixteen and played the trumpet in it for forty years.
After dinner their grandmother sat at the piano and entertained the family with a few old waltzes.
The busker outside the station was playing the saxophone for spare change.
She took up the violin again last year and hopes to improve her bowing.
The drummer spent the whole winter practising his rolls on a rubber pad.
quiet: Every evening the old sailor sat on the quay mending the nets for anyone who would pay.
My cousin runs the hill path for an hour a day because she wants to build her stamina.
A young woman stood by the fountain feeding the pigeons and checking her watch.
He joined the town club at sixteen and played rugby for it for twenty years.
After dinner their grandmother sat at the table and beat the family at a few hands of whist.
The vendor outside the station was selling hot chestnuts for spare change.
She took up tennis again last year and hopes to win a local match.
The carpenter spent the whole winter sanding the hull of a wooden boat.

notes: Card: ' playing' x3, ' played' x2, ' play' x2, 演奏, ' improve' x2, ' good' x2, all about musicians.
